title: How do we subtract one expression from another?
description: Six pairs of expressions are subtracted by writing the second expression, then minus the bracket of the first. The minus sign before the bracket changes every sign inside it.
teaching_notes: One idea: taking away a bracket changes every sign inside it. Watch for students who change only the first sign inside the bracket.

video_script.why: A learner uses the method of opening a bracket: the sign before the bracket acts on every term inside it, and then like terms are joined.
video_script.substitution: The method of opening a bracket such as two times the bracket y minus one, with a minus sign before the bracket in place of the number two.
video_script.anchor: six pairs of expressions where the first is taken away from the second
video_script.payoff_line: Every pair has now been subtracted

final_answer.spoken: minus three eigh plus fifteen b minus thirty two; eighteen x plus sixteen y minus twenty three; ten h minus twenty seven g plus two; minus three eigh minus three b minus thirty two; minus thirteen x minus thirteen y plus six; three h minus sixteen g plus thirty

maths_rules: subtracting A from B means B - (A); the minus sign changes every sign in A
video_script.design: One idea: write the second expression, then minus the bracket of the first, and let the minus sign change every sign inside. Assumes the example of opening a bracket. The six pairs stay on the stage.
open_questions: The book prints some answers in a different order of terms (for example 10h − 27g + 2 for the third); the video follows the worklist order, and the terms are equal.

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, six pairs of expressions in the letters eigh, b, x, y, g and h.

beats.on_screen: To find: the second expression minus the first, for each pair
narration: <bookmark mark='fd'/>We subtract in every pair. We work the same way as the example in your book.

marks.s1a: the second expression is written, then minus the bracket of the first
marks.s1b: every sign inside the bracket flips

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>First, the first pair. We write six eigh plus nine b minus eighteen. Then we write minus the bracket nine eigh minus six b plus fourteen.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>The minus sign changes every sign inside the bracket. It becomes minus nine eigh plus six b minus fourteen.

<bookmark mark='s1c'/>Six eigh minus nine eigh is minus three eigh. Nine b plus six b is fifteen b. <bookmark mark='s1d'/>Minus eighteen minus fourteen is minus thirty two. The answer is minus three eigh plus fifteen b minus thirty two.

marks.s2a: the bracket is written with a minus sign before it, and its signs flip

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Second, the second pair. Flip every sign in the bracket being taken away.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Three x plus fifteen x is eighteen x, and seven y plus nine y is sixteen y.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>Minus ten minus thirteen is minus twenty three. The answer is eighteen x plus sixteen y minus twenty three.

marks.s3a: the bracket is taken away and its signs flip

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Third, the third pair. Taking away seventeen g plus nine minus seven h flips all three signs.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Minus ten g minus seventeen g is minus twenty seven g. Three h plus seven h is ten h.
<bookmark mark='s3c'/>Eleven minus nine is two. The answer is ten h minus twenty seven g plus two.

marks.s4a: the bracket in the second expression is opened
marks.s4b: the first expression is taken away and its signs flip
marks.s4d: the b terms are joined and the answer is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Fourth, open the bracket in the second expression of the fourth pair first. It becomes six eigh minus nine b minus eighteen.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Then we take away nine eigh minus six b plus fourteen, so its signs flip.
<bookmark mark='s4c'/>Six eigh minus nine eigh is minus three eigh. <bookmark mark='s4d'/>Minus nine b plus six b is minus three b. The answer is minus three eigh minus three b minus thirty two.

marks.s5a: the fifth pair is worked with signs flipped
marks.s5b: the sixth pair is worked with signs flipped

narration: <bookmark mark='s5a'/>Fifth, the last two pairs. In the fifth, minus three x minus ten x is minus thirteen x. <bookmark mark='s5c'/>Minus three y minus ten y is minus thirteen y. <bookmark mark='s5d'/>Eight minus two is six, so the answer is minus thirteen x minus thirteen y plus six.

<bookmark mark='s5b'/>In the sixth, seven h minus four h is three h. <bookmark mark='s5e'/>Minus eight g minus eight g is minus sixteen g. <bookmark mark='s5f'/>Twenty plus ten is thirty, giving three h minus sixteen g plus thirty.

marks.s6a: 1 replaces eigh and b in the first pair
marks.s6b: the two expressions give minus 3 and 17
marks.s6c: the answer minus 20 matches the formula

narration: <bookmark mark='s6a'/>Sixth, check the first pair with eigh as one and b as one.
<bookmark mark='s6b'/>The second expression gives six plus nine minus eighteen, which is minus three. The first gives nine minus six plus fourteen, which is seventeen.
<bookmark mark='s6c'/>Minus three minus seventeen is minus twenty. Minus three plus fifteen minus thirty two is also minus twenty.
